name: Judas Maccabeus
description: Son of Mattathias, called Maccabeus; named by his father on his deathbed as captain to fight the battle of the people; rose up in his father's stead, slew Apollonius and Seron, cleansed and dedicated the sanctuary, campaigned in Idumea, Ammon and Galaad, made a league with Rome, and was killed in battle against Bacchides

points: The fear of Judas and his brethren fell on the nations round about them, and an exceeding great dread. When we go out and do this work, that is what falls on the nations.
They heard what Judas and Jonathan were doing and wanted a name of their own.
Nobody sent them. The spirit was on Judas and Jonathan, not on them, and they went under the guise of good intentions.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: The king sent Nicanor, one of his honourable princes, a man that bare deadly hate unto Israel, with commandment to destroy the people. He came to Judas and his brethren deceitfully with friendly words: let there be no battle between me and you; I will come with a few men, that I may see you in peace. But the enemies were prepared to take away Judas by violence. When Judas knew he came with deceit, he was afraid of him and would see his face no more.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Judas Maccabeus and they that were with him went privily into the towns, called their kinsfolk together, and took unto them all such as continued in the Jews' religion. There it is again: the Jews' religion.

note.label: In Vain Do They Worship Me! Religious Syncretism

points: Then the heathen that had fled out of Judea from Judas came to Nicanor by flocks, thinking the harm and calamities of the Jews to be their welfare.

note.label: The Pit and Pendulum: The Slow Genocide of the Undesired

points: This is the more detailed account of the same event. Nicanor came into the great and holy temple and commanded the priests to deliver him the man. When they sware they could not tell where he was, he stretched out his right hand toward the temple and made an oath: if ye will not deliver me Judas as a prisoner, I will lay this temple of God even with the ground, and I will break down the altar, and erect a notable temple unto Bacchus. He swore to put another god's temple in its place.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Judas, who was ever the chief defender of the citizens, commanded to strike off Nicanor's head, and his hand with his shoulder, the arm he had stretched out against the temple, and bring them to Jerusalem.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time
